column1: # boru Language Specification: module-system edge cases II
# trailing body code, namespace re-export), module bodies that
# fail, minted types crossing the boundary with their constructors,
# the unpack module forms, and the builtin wrappers' numeric /

column3: a duplicate export name inside ONE module: last wins
body statements after an export still run; the export stands

column1: import module [def a 1 end def b 2 end export "M" {s: (a add b)}] M.s
column3: `end`-separated body statements sequence like any program
each namespace carries its own $name
a pair-renamed binding keeps the DECLARED export name

column1: import module [import module [export "I" {v: 40}] export "O" {I: I}] O.I.v
column3: a namespace itself can be re-exported — the inner namespace rides out whole

column1: def m (module [export "MM" {v: 1}]) import m end import m end MM.v
column3: importing the same Module value twice is idempotent
a raise in the module body aborts the import with the body's code
a native error in the body aborts the import the same way

column1: # §3  minted types cross with their constructors
import module [def Age (refine Integer) export "M" {Age: Age}] M.Age istype
column3: an exported newtype is a first-class type importer-side

column3: …and a NOMINAL mint, distinct from its base type

column1: import module [def P class {x:Integer} export "M" {P: P}] make M.P {x:3} dot x eq 3
column3: an exported class constructs importer-side via make

column1: # §4  unpack — module words without the namespace

column3: unpack binds a module's words bare
…all of them
unpack does NOT bind the namespace — only the bare words
the export-named unpack form works for any builtin

column1: # §5  builtin wrappers — rounding family at the halves and negatives

column3: floor moves toward -inf
ceil moves toward +inf
round halves go AWAY from zero…
…in both directions
trunc moves toward zero
sign of zero is zero
min of negatives
log2 of one
the constant words are 0-arg exports
…fired transparently on access
sig order: atan2 x y — the SECOND operand is the ordinate
three-arg wrapper: a mul b add c, in source order
wrappers compose like any words

column1: # §6  builtin wrappers — string vocabulary under edge operands

column3: concat takes the LIST form, not two bare strings
indexof is needle-first, haystack-last
contains is needle-first too…
…GOTCHA: swapped operands quietly answer the wrong question
case mapping is Unicode-aware
non-Boolean operands go through truthiness (1 and 2 are truthy)
nor is order-free
two trues agree
iff of two falses holds

column1: # §8  module fns — arity, templates, and higher-order use
import module [def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] export "M" {f3: f3/v}] M.f3 1 2 3
column3: three forward args bind in source order

column1: import module [def f3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [((a mul 100) add (b mul 10)) add c]] export "M" {f3: f3/v}] 1 2 3 M.f3
column3: GOTCHA all-stack: sig position 0 is top of stack — the order reverses

column1: import module [def greet fn [[nm:String] [String] [`hi ${nm}`]] export "M" {greet: greet/v}] M.greet "bob"
column3: a template string in a module fn body interpolates module-side

column1: import module [def inc fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x add 1]] export "M" {inc: inc/v}] [1 2 3] each [M.inc]
column3: a module fn drives a higher-order body

column1: import module [export "M" {flag: true, nothing: none}] M.flag
column3: Boolean exports are plain values
an export value may be COMPUTED in the module body
duplicate export names collapse to one descriptor entry

column1: import module [def T (refine Integer) export "M" {a: 1}] T
column3: an unexported module TYPE stays private
renaming works on lowercase exports too
a multi-namespace builtin: each binding knows its own name
stack dispatch through a two-arg Float wrapper
binary exponent
GOTCHA sig order: IEEE remainder(4, 7) — the top-first convention again
max ignores a NaN operand
mixed-type min promotes and compares
pad right-fills with spaces to the width

column1: import module [def sq fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul x]] export "M" {sq: sq/v}] M.sq (M.sq 3)
column3: a module fn nests inside its own argument position
a later builtin import shadows an inline export of the same namespace

column1: import module [def v 1 export "M" {v: v} def v 2] M.v
column3: an export captures the value AT EXPORT TIME — a later body rebind is invisible
pair-renamed lowercase exports keep their declared $name
stack dispatch through a bin wrapper
GOTCHA sig order: nextafter steps 2.0 TOWARD 1.0 (top-first again)
a wrapper result feeds forward collection like any value
the `all` selector is for maps — module unpack has no such form

column1: # §12  a module fn's return contract is the frame's (NUR191, closed 2026-09-25)
import module [def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x 3]] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] M.d1 10
column3: a module fn leaving two values under a one-return contract raises the frame's count error — the CallBoru seam used to hand both back (`10 3`)

column1: import module [def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] []] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] M.d1 10
column3: …too few raises too

column1: import module [def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x 'a']] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] M.d1 10
column3: …and the count is checked before the types, as the frame checks it

column1: import module [def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer Integer] [x 3]] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] M.d1 10
column3: a two-return contract met is two values

column1: import module [def mk fn [[k:Integer] [Function] [([n:Integer] => [n add k])]] def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Function] [(mk x)]] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] 3 M.d1 10 typeof
column3: a module fn's single returned closure is PARKED where it lands, as a frame's return is — it used to re-step over the 3 (13)

column1: import module [def mk fn [[k:Integer] [Function] [([n:Integer] => [n add k])]] def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Function] [(mk x)]] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] ((M.d1 10) 3)
column3: …and the paren re-step applies it, as it applies any parked value

column1: import module [def mk fn [[k:Integer] [Function] [([n:Integer] => [n add k])]] def d1 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [(mk x) 3]] export "M" {d1: d1/v}] M.d1 10
column3: a factory's residual of a parked closure and a value is the count error the frame raises — the seam used to re-step the closure over the 3 (13)
